ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a parallel-type Zener diode voltage regulator circuit. The power supply on the left is labeled Vsource = 24 V; the power supply passes through the top series resistor Rseries, labeled in the figure as 1.2 kΩ; at the node, a Zener diode is connected downward, labeled Vz = 7.9 V; the load resistor Rload on the right is connected in parallel with the Zener diode to ground. Reasoning calculation: The problem gives Rload = 1 kΩ. According to the method, assume the Zener diode is in the voltage-regulating state, so the node voltage, namely the load voltage, is 7.9 V. The series resistor current is Iseries = (24 - 7.9) / 1.2 kΩ = 16.1 / 1200 A = 13.4167 mA. The load current is Iload = 7.9 / 1 kΩ = 7.9 mA. The Zener diode current is Izener = Iseries - Iload = 13.4167 - 7.9 = 5.5167 mA, which is 5.52 mA when kept to two decimal places.

Subtract the load current from the series current to get the zener current, then express it in mA.
